protocol_note: The official 13-question wording was not supplied in the isolation task and was not read before freezing. These are thirteen explicit, script-only narrative judgments, to be bound to the official schema without importing external story facts. Do not silently treat the criterion wording as a quotation of the official protocol.

answers.criterion: The opening establishes a concrete incident and an intelligible central puzzle
answers.evidence: s61001–s61003: the city has just heard one blast; within an hour people warn of a second, with the naval-yard powder magazine named.

answers.criterion: The opening gives the second warning meaningful human stakes
answers.evidence: s61004–s61005 asks whether injured evacuees can get safety news and shelter, and whether rescue continues after people set down tools.

answers.criterion: The script gives a clear question that can be answered by the end
answers.evidence: s61007 asks whether fire was dangerously close to the magazine or somebody misheard; s61040 and s61095–s61097 answer with Prince's account of actual fire danger and no second explosion.

answers.criterion: The setup gives enough cause for the first explosion without losing the second-warning thread
answers.evidence: s61010–s61024 explains the Mont-Blanc/Imo collision, explosive cargo, fire, crew escape, and roughly twenty-minute interval; s61034–s61039 returns to the magazine danger.

answers.criterion: Consequences are presented in a trackable cause-and-effect sequence
answers.evidence: s61025–s61126 moves from blast to damaged streets and cut communications; s61030–s61035 moves from firefighting losses to the next alarm; s61040–s61043 moves from magazine fire to evacuation.

answers.criterion: People make consequential choices rather than simply witness disaster
answers.evidence: s61043 has rescuers leave tools and take families away; s61057 has an artillery unit volunteer to flood the magazine; s61060–s61061 has a civic official take command and firefighters stay.

answers.criterion: Specific, visualizable details carry the story
answers.evidence: s61121–s61122 describes seawater carrying boats and debris onto land; s61043 names hammers, shovels, and bandages; s61063 describes people burning branches while awaiting word.

answers.criterion: A material complication or reversal changes what people are trying to do
answers.evidence: s61108 sends rescue vehicles north, then s61111 says the crowd is ordered south; s61052 says evacuation does not itself solve the magazine danger.

answers.criterion: The story keeps the geography and timing understandable
answers.evidence: s61010 marks the backward move with '稍早'; s61020 states about twenty minutes between collision and blast; s61127 says first medical landing was within fifteen minutes after the blast; s61111 contrasts northward rescue with southward evacuation.

answers.criterion: Question beats are used selectively and do not become repetitive
answers.evidence: s61034, s61037, and s61039 ask successive danger/alarm questions before the s61040 answer; s61062 and s61065 add more questions to the wait for safety news. The pattern recurs even where the next answer follows immediately.

answers.criterion: The narrator distinguishes direct record, quotation, and inference
answers.evidence: s61017 says Prince did not adjudicate full collision fault; s61041 gives no exact fire distance; s61045 labels household detail as Prince's quoted contemporary description; s61097 limits the artillery attribution to Prince's 1920 account and says military files were not separately checked.

answers.criterion: The central warning receives a definite payoff rather than remaining a tease
answers.evidence: s61066 brings the all-clear to the commons; s61095 explicitly says the second explosion did not happen; s61096 explains Prince's attribution to the artillery unit flooding the magazine.

answers.criterion: The ending follows through on the human aftermath it opened
answers.evidence: s61004–s61005 raises safety news, shelter, and rescue; s61066 and s61095–s61096 settle the alarm, but s61068–s61081 gives only brief search assignments and tents before the outro, with no concrete person or rescued group revisited.
